title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): X is a stratified space with strata X_i^* indexed by a poset I. The closure of a stratum is X_i = ⋃_{j≤i} X_j^*. Each stratum X_i^* has a tubular neighbourhood V_i, and for a flag i_0<…<i_n one sets V_{i_0…i_n} = V_{i_0}∩…∩V_{i_n}. The system (V_{i_0…i_n}) is an inductive system indexed by Drap(I)^op. For a locally closed Z the relative neighbourhoods V^Z = V∩Z are homotopy equivalent to the absolute ones (formulas 55–57). For J ⊂ I, X_J^* = ⋃_{i∈J} X_i^* and X_J = ⋃_{i∈J} X_i (formula 58).

This page does three things.
(1) If J is an 'idéal' (downward closed), then X_J^* = X_J, which is closed.
(2) If J is a 'tranche' (order-convex), equivalently J' = J̃∖J is an ideal, where J̃ is the down-closure of J, then X_J^* = X_{J̃}^* ∖ X_{J'}^* (59). It is therefore a difference of two closed sets, hence locally closed. The sets X_i^J = X_i ∩ X_J^* (i∈J) give a stratification of Z = X_J^* indexed by J.
(3) Set V^J_{j_0…j_n} = V_{j_0…j_n} ∩ X_J^* (60). These are the tubular-neighbourhood data of the induced J-stratification of Z. Consequently Z ≃ lim→ over pairs i,j∈J of (V_i^J, V_ij^J), i.e. ≃ lim→ over Drap(J) of V^J_{i_0…i_n} (61).

Meaning of (61): the V_i^J form an open cover of Z, and the intersections of non-comparable V_i are empty. The Čech nerve of the cover therefore reduces to the flag-indexed diagram, and Z is its (homotopy) colimit. The purpose is to localize the 'déploiement' construction to convex pieces of the stratification. On the next page this is used to define pro-tubular neighbourhoods V(X_J^*, X_{J'}^*) of one convex piece inside a larger one, J ⊂ J'.
errors: No substantive error. The claimed equivalence between 'tranche' (convex) and 'J̃∖J is an ideal' is correct in both directions.

Minor notation: in (61) the pairs should be restricted to comparable i≤j (or i<j). The lim→ must be read as a homotopy colimit, or as an honest colimit of an open cover; the 2-term notation (V_i, V_ij) is shorthand for the Čech-type diagram.
Implicit hypothesis: (61) needs the V_i^J to cover Z and V_i∩V_j = ∅ for incomparable i,j. This is presumably part of the tubular-system axioms fixed earlier but is not restated here.

ideas.what: Unions of strata indexed by down-sets are closed; those indexed by order-convex subsets are locally closed and inherit a stratification indexed by the subposet
ideas.modern_name: Locally closed unions of strata over convex subposets (standard in stratified spaces / recollement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used systematically in BBD 1982 and in stratified homotopy theory (e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A)

ideas.what: A stratified space is the colimit of the flag-indexed diagram of intersections of tubular neighbourhoods of strata
ideas.modern_name: Čech/hocolim decomposition over the nerve of an open cover; flag-indexed diagram of neighbourhoods (cf. Quinn's homotopy links, exit-path category)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968), Dugger–Isaksen for hocolim of covers; Quinn (1988) and Lurie for stratified versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces but gives no such formulas

ideas.what: Relative tubular systems: restricting the neighbourhood system to a convex piece Z = X_J^* gives the tubular system of the induced J-stratification
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of stratified neighbourhood data / control data to locally closed unions of strata

deep.surprise_reason: A routine bookkeeping page: convex subposets give locally closed sub-stratified spaces, and the Čech-type colimit formula is restricted to them. This is standard material, setting up the pro-tubular neighbourhoods on the next page; nothing here is novel.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 'i∈J, j<i ⇒ j∈J' (the 'i' is slightly overwritten); this is consistent with the transcription.
In (61) the indexing is written 'i,j ∈ J' under lim→ and '(i_0,…,i_n) ∈ Drap(J)' below; the second lim→ shows (V^J_{i_0…i_n}), as transcribed.
Margin note under (59) reads approximately 'différence de deux parties fermées, c'est une partie localement fermée de X'; this is correct.
